title: Glimmerpine: a cozy Christmas game I've been making with Claude Code over the past couple of months (free browser demo!)
author: toni_btrain
selftext:
I've been building this with Claude Code for the last couple months, and [the demo went up on itch today](https://kafana-studio.itch.io/glimmerpine), so this felt like the right place to share it.

It's a Christmas tree decorating game. You inherit your grandma's cabin in a village where the candles went out years ago, the neighbours write you letters asking for trees, and every tree you light brings a house back. Each ornament you hang plays the next note of a carol.

How it was made, roughly:

* The game itself was my job: the idea, the world, the story and the characters, and the whole look and feel. I made every design call, played it constantly, reviewed every screen and every scene, and sent things back again and again until they felt right. A lot of what makes it feel the way it does came out of that back and forth.
* Claude wrote pretty much all of the code (TypeScript, Three.js and Preact, about 130k lines by now), working from that direction.
* There are no 3D model files at all. The trees, the houses, the villagers and the train station are all built in code, which is also why the browser build is small.
* The music is written in code too. Claude built a small Python toolkit for composing, and the 30-odd tracks are scored in it, mostly arrangements of old public-domain carols plus a few original themes.
* The trailer is rendered by the game itself: a script poses the camera and the characters, renders frame by frame, and the cuts land on the beats of a score written for it.
* The painted 2D art (the character portraits and the logo) came from an image model, then got picked, edited and fitted in.
* Around 90 test files, plus bots that play whole chapters through the real UI. They caught a surprising number of bugs.

The biggest lesson: Claude can build almost anything you describe, but it can't tell on its own when something looks or feels off. That part stayed my job the whole way through. What worked was a tight loop of render it, look at it, say exactly what's wrong, repeat. Screenshots and before/after images did far more than long descriptions.

Demo (plays in the browser, about 40 min): [https://kafana-studio.itch.io/glimmerpine](https://kafana-studio.itch.io/glimmerpine)  
The full game comes to Steam in December.
